question: What is the exact public API surface? answer: Three points, no more. To maintain compatibility with existing legacy systems, your public entry surface must be strictly set to: ConnectionPool.new(size:, timeout:, &block); pool.with { |conn| ... }; pool.with_connection { |conn| ... }; ConnectionPool.wrap(size:, timeout:, &block); wrapper.respond_to?(name). You can decide the internal implementation logic yourself. On the proxy class: the Wrapper class responds to :with and :with_connection as its own methods (METHODS = [:with, :with_connection]). For any other name it delegates to the pooled resource's respond_to?. On the re-entrancy reference: that phrase resolves to the per-thread stack mechanism in lib/connection_pool.rb — each thread holds a stack (keyed by object_id of the queue), pushing on checkout and popping on checkin. Re-entrant borrows push the same connection again; the resource is only returned to the pool when the outermost borrow completes (stack becomes empty). Too many questions. answer: Accepted — 'reentrancy' is a concrete name.
